rule.title: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63 (Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.): Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rule.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels, and unlawful for landlords to use one. Each month of violation and each dwelling unit is a separate violation.
rule.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rule.penalty: City Attorney or aggrieved tenant may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits (City Attorney) and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing party gets reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
rule.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63; Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.
rule.status_basis: Document shows the ordinance was passed to print on 2025-11-18 and was on the 2025-12-02 council agenda; adoption and effective dates are not stated.

rule.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rule.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or tenancy decisions, including refusing to rent, demanding higher deposits or rent, or disqualifying people from rental assistance. Before taking any adverse action based on criminal history, the landlord must give written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rule.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages (actual damages or three times one month's rent), punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rule.status_basis: Berkeley City Council passed the ordinance on April 14, 2020; effective date not stated.

rule.requirement: Owners must pay tenants relocation assistance for an owner move-in eviction. The payment is indexed to inflation and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase; for 2026 the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471.

rule.title: California Civil Code Section 1950.6 (tenant screening fees)
rule.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee up to a state-set maximum, and must provide a receipt, an itemized list of expenses, a copy of the credit report, and a refund of any unused portion. No fee may be charged if no unit is available, and a reusable screening report must be accepted.

rule.title: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.78 (Tenant Screening and Application Fees)
rule.requirement: Owners who charge a screening fee must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and state the maximum fee cap under Civil Code 1950.6(b) before receiving the fee. Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy or for adding, replacing or removing a roommate. The chapter applies to all residential rental agreements, and any contrary lease provision is unenforceable.

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley regardless of contrary lease language.

rule.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rule.title: Measure BB (Berkeley Rent Ordinance amendments) – just cause eviction changes
rule.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units can be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for nonpayment where the debt is under one month of Fair Market Rent, and for failing to sign a new lease. Lease-breach evictions require substantial actual harm and unreasonable tenant behavior, and notices must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days.

rule.status_basis: Passed by voters in the November 2024 election.

rule.title: Measure BB (Berkeley Rent Ordinance amendments) – Annual General Adjustment cap
rule.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment, the yearly amount a landlord of a fully covered unit may raise rent, is set by a CPI-based formula but capped at 5%. rule.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act: violations (Common pricing algorithms)
rule.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term. Complaints need only plausibly allege a contract, combination or conspiracy.
rule.penalty: Violations of the Cartwright Act are punishable as a crime; the bill states it creates a new crime or infraction.
rule.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (added by AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rule.status_basis: Approved by Governor October 06, 2025; the chunk states no effective date.

coverage.summary: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, across all products and services, not only housing.
coverage.exemptions_summary: The term 'person' does not include the end consumer of a product or service.

precedence.text: Nothing in this section shall impair or limit the applicability of antitrust laws.

rule.title: California Civil Code section 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act of 2019 – just cause)
rule.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without stating a just cause (at-fault or no-fault) in the written notice. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance (within 15 days of notice) or waive the final month's rent.

rule.penalty: Non-compliant notice is void; owner liable for actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages (plus punitive damages) for willful or malicious violations; injunctive relief by Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel.

rule.title: Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 186, Section 15B (security deposits and rental advances)
rule.requirement: When a lessor transfers the property, the lessor stays liable for the held rental advance and its interest until it is credited to the successor and the tenant is notified in writing, or until it is credited to the tenant with accrued interest paid. rule.title: Reprisal for reporting violations of law or for tenant's union activity (G.L. c. 186, § 18)
rule.requirement: Landlords and their agents may not threaten or take reprisals against a residential tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations, or organizing or joining a tenants' union. A termination of tenancy (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal, and the landlord can rebut this only by clear and convincing evidence.
rule.key_value: Six-month rebuttable presumption; damages of one to three months' rent or actual damages, whichever is greater
rule.penalty: Liable for damages of not less than one month's rent nor more than three months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

requires.name: residential_tenancy

rule.title: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B (limits on upfront charges by lessors)
rule.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a lessor may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock-change fee. Application, screening, pet, cleaning and amenity fees are forbidden for landlords.

rule.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rule.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rents. Software providers and other coordinators may not use such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords.
rule.penalty: Attorney general must establish a complaint portal for alleged violations; existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act are preserved.

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rule.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record until after a conditional offer. They may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer, they may consider only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods, and a withdrawal needs an individualized assessment and written notice.

rule.penalty: Civil penalty up to $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 for a second within five years, and $10,000 for two or more others within seven years; the director may also order the application fee returned and up to $1,000 paid to the applicant.
rule.status_basis: Takes effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment (approved June 18, 2021).

rule.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rule.requirement: Landlords may collect a security deposit of no more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and annual increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Deposits must be held in trust in an interest-bearing account, interest belongs to the tenant, and the tenant must receive written notice of the bank and account details within 30 days.

rule.penalty: If the tenant does not receive proper notice or interest, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% per annum interest to rent.

A landlord who wrongfully withholds a deposit may owe double the amount withheld plus costs and attorney's fees.

rule.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy (San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7)
rule.requirement: Landlords must give tenants notice of protections, and for at-fault terminations give notice and opportunity to cure. For no-fault terminations they must give written notice stating the basis, pay relocation assistance (direct payment or rent waiver), and offer to re-lease within five years. Landlords must notify the Commission, and failure to comply voids the termination notice. Buyout agreements are regulated and cannot be for less than the relocation assistance.

rule.penalty: Termination notice void; damages of not less than three times actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; not less than three times required relocation assistance plus actual damages; punitive damages; attorney's fees and costs in court's discretion; City enforcement with civil and criminal remedies.
